goals.title: Can an arrival list shorten the reading room queue?
goals.description: This fictional pilot shows how the same logbook can track a different project. A small library wants to help booked visitors get seated sooner.
path: Record the wait from arrival to seating under both methods.
Keep the outcome, the reason for the decision, and the next measurement together.
files: Shows how to reuse the logbook structure for another project.

goals.title: Measure the wait
goals.description: How long did visitors wait under each sign-in method?

story.tried: Record four waits for a paper list and four for a prepared arrival list.
story.found: The fictional medians were 8 and 4 minutes, respectively.
story.next: Review whether the methods were tested under comparable conditions.
story.source: Fictional observations supplied with this example.

files: Lists the individual waits used in the comparison.
Recomputes the two medians from the CSV.

goals.title: Review the decision
goals.description: The shorter wait is promising enough to justify a better comparison.

story.tried: Compare the medians with the session notes and check what the trial controlled.
story.found: The arrival list ran in the afternoon and the paper list ran in the morning. Time of day may explain the difference.
story.next: Alternate sign-in methods in matching time slots and record both visitor and staff time.

files: Records the follow-up and why the draft rollout decision changed.
